title: Update Termux packages
summary: Refresh package lists and upgrade everything before installing tools.
objective: Bring a fresh Termux installation up to date so later installs do not fail.
prerequisites: Termux installed from F-Droid or the official GitHub releases

steps.title: Update and upgrade
steps.explanation: pkg update refreshes the package index; pkg upgrade installs newer versions. Answer y to prompts, or add -y.

steps.title: Pick a faster mirror if needed
steps.explanation: Opens a menu to choose a mirror. Use it if downloads fail or are very slow.

expectedResult: The command finishes without errors and pkg list-installed shows current versions.

troubleshooting.fix: Run termux-change-repo, choose a mirror, then pkg update again.

troubleshooting.problem: Repository is under maintenance or down

warnings: Termux is not a rooted Linux system: do not use sudo. Use pkg for Termux packages.
Play Store builds of Termux are outdated; use F-Droid or the official GitHub releases.

title: Install Node.js and npm in Termux
summary: Install Node.js, check versions, and run a first script.
objective: Run JavaScript and use npm on your Android device.
prerequisites: Updated Termux packages (see the update tutorial)

steps.title: Install Node.js
steps.explanation: Installs node and npm from the Termux repository (LTS variant).

steps.title: Check versions
steps.explanation: Confirms both tools are on your PATH.

steps.title: Create and run a script
steps.command: echo 'console.log("hello from Termux")' > hello.js && node hello.js
steps.explanation: Writes a one-line script and runs it.

troubleshooting.problem: npm install fails building a native module
troubleshooting.fix: Install build tools: pkg install build-essential python, then retry. Some modules do not support Android/ARM.
Do not use sudo. Install packages inside your project folder in your home directory.

warnings: Packaged Node versions can lag behind nodejs.org. Check node -v against your project's engines field.

title: Use GitHub with SSH in Termux
summary: Create an SSH key and connect Termux to GitHub.
objective: Clone and push to GitHub without typing a password.

steps.title: Generate a key
steps.explanation: Creates ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 (private) and id_ed25519.pub (public). Set a passphrase.

steps.title: Show the public key
steps.explanation: Copy this output and add it under GitHub, Settings, SSH and GPG keys. Never share the file without .pub.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.explanation: Confirm the GitHub fingerprint on first use. GitHub should greet you by username.

expectedResult: Cloning works without a password prompt.

troubleshooting.fix: Check that the key was added to your GitHub account and run ssh -vT git@github.com to see which key is offered.

warnings: Never paste your private key anywhere. Only the .pub file is shared.

title: Access shared Android storage
summary: Let Termux read and write Downloads and other shared folders.
objective: Move files between Android apps and your Termux projects.

steps.title: Request permission
steps.explanation: Android shows a permission prompt. Allow it.

steps.title: Inspect the links
steps.explanation: You should see links such as downloads, dcim and shared.

steps.title: Copy a file in
steps.explanation: Copies from Downloads into a project folder.

expectedResult: Files in Downloads are visible in ~/storage/downloads.

troubleshooting.fix: Re-run termux-setup-storage, or enable storage permission for Termux in Android app settings.

warnings: Keep Git repositories in the Termux home directory. Shared storage does not support Unix permissions or symlinks properly and can break tools.

title: Run long-running processes in Termux
summary: Keep a dev server alive and understand Android's background limits.
objective: Run a server in the background and reduce the chance Android stops it.
prerequisites: A Node.js or Python app to run

steps.title: Acquire a wake lock
steps.explanation: Asks Android to keep Termux awake. Release with termux-wake-unlock.

steps.title: Start the server in the background
steps.explanation: & runs it in the background; output goes to server.log.

steps.title: Check and stop it
steps.explanation: jobs lists background jobs. Stop one with kill %1.

expectedResult: The server responds on localhost while Termux is running.

troubleshooting.problem: Process killed when the screen is off
troubleshooting.fix: Disable battery optimization for Termux in Android settings. Vendor behavior varies and cannot be guaranteed.

warnings: Android may stop background apps at any time. Do not rely on Termux for production hosting.
